# Chapel choir recording

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina, **Kyrie — Missa Sicut lilium inter spinas**, performed by **The Tudor Consort**. Recording licensed **CC BY 3.0**.

- Recording and licence authority: https://freemusicarchive.org/music/The_Tudor_Consort/Renaissance_influences_-_Pizzetti_Messa_di_Requiem__Palestrina_Missa_Sicut_lilium_inter_spinas/02_Kyrie_-_Missa_Sicut_lilium_inter_spinas/
- Licence: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
- Original MP3 SHA256: `9aba8d0c204a8c705b5a52c0f056a492df267834349026e57cfc7ef66733dd68`.
- Original track page checked 2026-10-25; the original recording's embedded copyright tag corroborates the track page.
- Adaptation: first Kyrie section (0–80.1 seconds), mono downmix, gain raised 3 dB, 25 ms entry and 400 ms quiet-boundary fades, padded to 88 seconds. Original performed pitches and timing retained. Runtime splits this one recording into continuous natural and gain-modulated projection paths, with spatial filtering and procedural reflections.

This is a **five-part SATTB work in one recorded ensemble mix**, not five or six isolated singers. Shared amplification is provisional; it cannot establish independent six-voice musical behaviour. No stereo source separation, pitch cloning or synthesized singing was used. A suitable independent six-part recording and its permission remain pending.

The source build and game credits use `src/data/chapel-choir.js`; `tools/chunk_surfer/build-chapel-choir.mjs` requires the original recording hash before making the derivative. The built manifest records the actual derivative hash.

Marcoll's publicly distributed Max patch and staging instructions were inspected as reference, not shipped, executed or copied. His recordings and absent piece-specific automation are not game assets. Our modulation progression is original and does not claim to reproduce his work.
